title: Mansa Musa — the pilgrimage that broke a currency
style: documentary photograph, 14th century West Africa and Egypt, warm desert light, muted earth and gold, fine grain, period-accurate, no text, no watermark, no modern objects
$note: SIX LINES, EIGHTY WORDS, THIRTY SECONDS. The reference reel is six scenes in thirty seconds and its whole script is seventy-seven words; the draft this replaces was nine lines and a hundred and eighty-four, which is sixty-eight seconds of narration and the reason every cut felt slow and every shot felt empty. A line that will not fit in fifteen words is two lines or it is cut. EVERY LINE NAMES A REAL THING — the Catalan Atlas exists and is photographed, so imageCommons carries the search and the prompt only draws the nameless scenery.

lines.vo: This is the only picture anyone drew of him, and they never met.
lines.image: an old vellum chart on a wooden table, dividers and an inkpot beside it
lines.artefact: a detail of a medieval illuminated map on vellum, gold leaf and faded ink, cracked surface
caption: Drawn by
someone who
never met him.

lines.vo: In thirteen twenty-four the king of Mali set out for Mecca with his treasury.
lines.image: an old hand-drawn chart of north and west Africa on vellum, faded ink

lines.vo: The caravan was so long that accounts still argue about the number.
lines.image: a wide desert horizon at midday, heat haze over flat sand, empty
pieces: traveller in a long desert robe

lines.vo: He reached the holy city with an empire of gold still on his camels.
lines.image: a great stone courtyard under a hard white sun, colonnades in deep shadow
lines.artefact: a black draped cube in the centre of a vast stone court, seen from above

lines.vo: In Cairo he did not sell it. He gave it away, and the price of gold collapsed.
lines.image: an empty medieval Cairo market street of pale stone at noon, deep shadow under arches

lines.vo: It had not recovered twelve years later. The most expensive journey in history.
lines.image: a single set of footprints crossing an empty dune, wind erasing them
lines.title: TWELVE YEARS
lines.footer: the most expensive journey in history
